ten: SPEAKING PART 3: LẬP LUẬN TRỪU TƯỢNG

bang.Part 3: về xã hội, xu hướng, tương lai

bang_ngu_phap.ten: Dàn ý PREP — dùng cho mọi câu Part 3

bang.Cụm mở: I’d say that… · On balance, I think…
This is mainly because… · The main reason is that…
Take X for example… · In my country, for instance…
So overall… · That said, it does depend on…

bang_ngu_phap.ten: Sáu loại câu hỏi Part 3 và cách xử lý

bang.Cách trả lời: Whereas people used to…, now they…
The main driver is… · This largely stems from…
It’s likely that… · I imagine that in the long run…
On the one hand… on the other… · The benefits arguably outweigh…
One effective measure would be to…

bang.Ví dụ câu hỏi: *Some people say X. What do you think?*
bang.Cách trả lời: While it’s true that…, I’d argue that…

bang_ngu_phap.ten: Bốn tiêu chí chấm và cách cải thiện nhanh nhất

bang.Cải thiện nhanh nhất: dùng PREP, dùng từ nối khi nói
học collocation theo chủ đề, dùng paraphrase
chèn 1–2 câu phức (mệnh đề quan hệ, điều kiện)

bang.Ý nghĩa: phát âm, trọng âm, ngữ điệu
bang.Cải thiện nhanh nhất: luyện đuôi -s/-ed, trọng âm từ, shadowing

luot.en: Do you think people rely too much on technology?

pa.cau: Do you think people rely too much on technology?
pa.ipa_noi: /də jə θɪŋk ˈpiːpəl rɪˈlaɪ tuː mʌtʃ‿ɑːn teˈknɑːlədʒiː/

luot.en: I’d say they probably do, at least in some areas of life. The main reason is that convenience tends to replace skills we used to have — take navigation for example: most people my age can’t read a paper map anymore because we’ve always had GPS. That said, I wouldn’t call this a serious problem in itself. Every generation loses certain skills and gains others. What concerns me more is the loss of concentration. Whereas people used to read long articles, now they tend to skim. In the long run, that may well affect how deeply we think about complex issues.
luot.vi: Đếm: câu trả lời này dùng PREP, 2 cụm hedging, 1 câu chẻ, 1 cấu trúc so sánh quá khứ–hiện tại. Đó là band 7.

pa.ipa_noi: /aɪ diː seɪ ðeɪ ˈprɑːbəˌbliː də ət liːst‿ɪn səm ˈeriːəz‿əv laɪf ðə meɪn ˈriːzən‿ɪz ðət kəˈnviːnjəns tendz tə rɪˈpleɪs skɪlz‿wiː juːzd tə həv teɪk ˈnævəˈɡeɪʃən fə ɪˈɡzæmpəl məʊst ˈpiːpəl maɪ eɪdʒ kən tiː red‿ə ˈpeɪpə mæp ˌeniːˈmɔː bɪˈkɔːz‿wiː viː ˈɔːˌlweɪz həd ˈɡiːpiːˈes ðət sed‿aɪ wouldn tiː kɔːl ðɪs‿ə ˈsɪriːəs ˈprɑːbləm‿ɪn ˌɪˈtself ˈevəriː ˌdʒenəˈreɪʃən ˈluːzəz ˈsɜːtən skɪlz‿ən ɡeɪnz ˈʌðəz‿wʌt kəˈnsɜːnz miː mɔː ɪz ðə lɔːs‿əv ˌkɑːnsəˈntreɪʃən‿weˈræz ˈpiːpəl‿juːzd tə red lɔːŋ ˈɑːtəkəlz naʊ ðeɪ tend tə skɪm‿ɪn ðə lɔːŋ rʌn ðət meɪ wel‿əˈfekt haʊ ˈdiːpliː wiː θɪŋk‿əˈbaʊt ˈkɑːmpleks ˈɪʃuːz/

luot.en: Should governments limit how much technology children use?
luot.vi: Chính phủ có nên giới hạn mức độ trẻ em dùng công nghệ không?

pa.cau: Should governments limit how much technology children use?
pa.ipa_noi: /ʃəd ˈɡʌvəmənts ˈlɪmət haʊ mʌtʃ teˈknɑːlədʒiː ˈtʃɪldrən‿juːs/

luot.en: In principle it sounds sensible, but enforcement would be almost impossible. The responsibility probably has to sit with parents and schools.
luot.vi: Về nguyên tắc nghe hợp lý, nhưng việc thực thi gần như bất khả thi. Trách nhiệm có lẽ phải thuộc về cha mẹ và nhà trường.

pa.cau: In principle it sounds sensible, but enforcement would be almost impossible. The responsibility probably has to sit with parents and schools.
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪn ˈprɪnsəpəl‿ɪt saʊndz ˈsensəbəl bət‿eˈnfɔːsmənt‿wəd biː ˈɔːˌlməʊst ˌɪˈmpɑːsəbəl ðə riːˌspɑːnsəˈbɪlətiː ˈprɑːbəˌbliː həz tə sɪt‿wɪð ˈpeərənts‿ən skuːlz/

luot.en: How might schools approach it?
luot.vi: Nhà trường có thể tiếp cận thế nào?

pa.cau: How might schools approach it?
pa.ipa_noi: /haʊ maɪt skuːlz‿əˈprəʊtʃ‿ɪt/

luot.en: By teaching judgement rather than imposing bans. A child who understands why something is harmful is far better protected than one who is simply forbidden.
luot.vi: Bằng cách dạy khả năng phán đoán thay vì áp lệnh cấm. Một đứa trẻ hiểu vì sao điều gì đó có hại được bảo vệ tốt hơn nhiều so với đứa chỉ bị cấm.

pa.cau: By teaching judgement rather than imposing bans. A child who understands why something is harmful is far better protected than one who is simply forbidden.
pa.ipa_noi: /baɪ ˈtiːtʃɪŋ ˈdʒʌdʒmənt ˈræðə ðən ˌɪˈmpəʊzɪŋ bænz‿ə tʃaɪld huː ˌʌndəˈstændz‿waɪ ˈsʌmθɪŋ‿ɪz ˈhɑːmfəl‿ɪz fɑː ˈbetə prəˈtektɪd ðən‿wʌn huː ɪz ˈsɪmpliː ˈfɔːbɪdən/

luot.en: Do you think this generation is more isolated than previous ones?
luot.vi: Bạn có nghĩ thế hệ này cô lập hơn các thế hệ trước không?

pa.cau: Do you think this generation is more isolated than previous ones?
pa.ipa_noi: /də jə θɪŋk ðɪs ˌdʒenəˈreɪʃən‿ɪz mɔː ˈaɪsəˌleɪtəd ðən ˈpriːviːəs‿wʌnz/

luot.en: That is often claimed, though I am not entirely convinced. They have fewer face-to-face friendships but far wider networks, which is a different kind of connection rather than none at all.
luot.vi: Điều đó thường được nêu, dù tôi không hoàn toàn bị thuyết phục. Họ có ít bạn bè gặp mặt hơn nhưng mạng lưới rộng hơn nhiều, đó là một dạng kết nối khác chứ không phải không có.

pa.cau: That is often claimed, though I am not entirely convinced. They have fewer face-to-face friendships but far wider networks, which is a different kind of connection rather than none at all.
pa.ipa_noi: /ðət‿ɪz ˈɔːfən kleɪmd ðəʊ aɪ əm nɑːt‿ɪˈntaɪəliː kəˈnvɪnst ðeɪ həv ˈfjuːə feɪs tə feɪs ˈfrendʃɪps bət fɑː ˈwaɪdə ˈneˌtwɜːks‿wɪtʃ‿ɪz‿ə ˈdɪfərənt kaɪnd‿əv kəˈnekʃən ˈræðə ðən nʌn‿ət‿ɔːl/

luot.en: What would change your mind?
luot.vi: Điều gì sẽ khiến bạn đổi ý?

pa.cau: What would change your mind?
pa.ipa_noi: /wʌt‿wəd tʃeɪndʒ‿jə maɪnd/

luot.en: Long-term evidence on mental health. At present most of the studies I have seen show correlation rather than cause.
luot.vi: Bằng chứng dài hạn về sức khỏe tâm thần. Hiện tại phần lớn nghiên cứu tôi từng đọc chỉ cho thấy tương quan chứ chưa phải nhân quả.

pa.cau: Long-term evidence on mental health. At present most of the studies I have seen show correlation rather than cause.
pa.ipa_noi: /lɔːŋ tɜːm ˈevədəns‿ɑːn ˈmentəl helθ‿ət ˈprezənt məʊst‿əv ðə ˈstʌdiːz‿aɪ həv siːn ʃəʊ ˌkɔːrəˈleɪʃən ˈræðə ðən kɑːz/

hoi_thoai.ten: Hội thoại 2 — Lập luận về vấn đề trừu tượng

luot.en: Is progress always a good thing?
luot.vi: Tiến bộ có luôn là điều tốt không?

pa.cau: Is progress always a good thing?
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪz ˈprɑːˌɡres ˈɔːˌlweɪz‿ə ɡʊd θɪŋ/

luot.en: It depends entirely on how we define it. If progress means efficiency alone, then a great deal is lost along the way.
luot.vi: Điều đó hoàn toàn tùy vào cách ta định nghĩa. Nếu tiến bộ chỉ có nghĩa là hiệu quả, thì rất nhiều thứ bị đánh mất dọc đường.

pa.cau: It depends entirely on how we define it. If progress means efficiency alone, then a great deal is lost along the way.
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪt dɪˈpendz‿ɪˈntaɪəliː ɑːn haʊ wiː dɪˈfaɪn‿ɪt‿ɪf ˈprɑːˌɡres miːnz‿ɪˈfɪʃnsi əˈləʊn ðen‿ə ɡreɪt diːl‿ɪz lɔːst‿əˈlɔːŋ ðə weɪ/

luot.en: Could you give an example?
luot.vi: Bạn cho một ví dụ được không?

pa.cau: Could you give an example?
pa.ipa_noi: /kə‿dʒə ɡɪv‿ən‿ɪˈɡzæmpəl/

luot.en: Agriculture, perhaps. Yields have risen enormously, yet soil quality in many regions has declined at the same time.
luot.vi: Có lẽ là nông nghiệp. Sản lượng tăng vọt, nhưng chất lượng đất ở nhiều vùng lại suy giảm cùng lúc.

pa.cau: Agriculture, perhaps. Yields have risen enormously, yet soil quality in many regions has declined at the same time.
pa.ipa_noi: /ˈæɡrɪˌkʌltʃə pəˈhæps‿jiːldz həv ˈrɪzən‿ɪˈnɔːməsliː jet sɔɪl ˈkwɑːlətiː ɪn ˈmeniː ˈriːdʒənz həz dɪˈklaɪnd‿ət ðə seɪm taɪm/

luot.en: Who should decide what counts as progress?
luot.vi: Ai nên quyết định thế nào là tiến bộ?

pa.cau: Who should decide what counts as progress?
pa.ipa_noi: /huː ʃəd dɪˈsaɪd‿wʌt kaʊnts‿əz ˈprɑːˌɡres/

luot.en: Ideally the people affected by it, although in practice the decision usually rests with whoever funds the change.
luot.vi: Lý tưởng là những người chịu tác động, dù trên thực tế quyết định thường thuộc về bên chi tiền cho sự thay đổi.

pa.cau: Ideally the people affected by it, although in practice the decision usually rests with whoever funds the change.
pa.ipa_noi: /aɪˈdiːliː ðə ˈpiːpəl‿əˈfektɪd baɪ ɪt ˌɔːˈlðəʊ ɪn ˈpræktəs ðə dɪˈsɪʒn ˈjuːʒuəli rests‿wɪð huːˈevə fʌndz ðə tʃeɪndʒ/

luot.en: Is that necessarily wrong?
luot.vi: Điều đó có nhất thiết là sai không?

pa.cau: Is that necessarily wrong?
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪz ðət ˌnesəˈserəliː rɔːŋ/

luot.en: Not inherently, provided there is some way of holding them accountable afterwards.
luot.vi: Không hẳn về bản chất, miễn là có cơ chế buộc họ chịu trách nhiệm về sau.

pa.cau: Not inherently, provided there is some way of holding them accountable afterwards.
pa.ipa_noi: /nɑːt‿ɪˈnhɪrəntliː prəˈvaɪdɪd ðə ɪz səm‿weɪ əv ˈhəʊldɪŋ ðəm‿əˈkaʊntəbəl ˈæftəwədz/

luot.en: How optimistic are you about the next twenty years?
luot.vi: Bạn lạc quan đến đâu về hai mươi năm tới?

pa.cau: How optimistic are you about the next twenty years?
pa.ipa_noi: /haʊ ˌɑːptəˈmɪstɪk‿ə jə əˈbaʊt ðə nekst ˈtwentiː jɪəz/

luot.en: Cautiously optimistic. Problems tend to be solved late rather than never, which is frustrating but not hopeless.
luot.vi: Lạc quan một cách thận trọng. Các vấn đề thường được giải quyết muộn chứ không phải không bao giờ, điều đó gây bực bội nhưng không tuyệt vọng.

pa.cau: Cautiously optimistic. Problems tend to be solved late rather than never, which is frustrating but not hopeless.
pa.ipa_noi: /ˈkɔːʃəsliː ˌɑːptəˈmɪstɪk ˈprɑːbləmz tend tə biː sɑːlvd leɪt ˈræðə ðən ˈnevə wɪtʃ‿ɪz ˈfrʌˌstreɪtɪŋ bət nɑːt ˈhəʊpləs/

hoi_thoai.ten: Hội thoại — Phát triển kinh tế

luot.en: Do you think city development helps everyone?
luot.vi: Bạn nghĩ sự phát triển đô thị có giúp ích cho mọi người không?

pa.cau: Do you think city development helps everyone?
pa.ipa_noi: /də jə θɪŋk ˈsɪtiː dɪˈveləpmənt helps ˈevriːˌwʌn/

luot.en: It is complex. Many people lose their homes.
luot.vi: Phức tạp lắm. Nhiều người mất nhà cửa.

pa.cau: It is complex. Many people lose their homes.
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪt‿ɪz ˈkɑːmpleks ˈmeniː ˈpiːpəl luːz ðeə həʊmz/

luot.en: True, but the economy grows with new offices.
luot.vi: Đúng, nhưng kinh tế phát triển nhờ các văn phòng mới.

pa.cau: True, but the economy grows with new offices.
pa.ipa_noi: /truː bət ðə ɪˈkɑːnəmiː ɡrəʊz‿wɪð nuː ˈɔːfəsəz/

luot.en: I agree, but we must use the PREP structure to analyze this.
luot.vi: Tôi đồng ý, nhưng chúng ta phải dùng cấu trúc PREP để phân tích việc này.

pa.cau: I agree, but we must use the PREP structure to analyze this.
pa.ipa_noi: /aɪ əˈɡriː bət‿wiː mʌs‿tʃuːs ðə prep ˈstrʌktʃə tə ˈænəˌlaɪz ðɪs/

luot.en: Point, Reason, Example, Point. Let us try.
luot.vi: Điểm chính, lý do, ví dụ, điểm chính. Thử xem nhé.

pa.cau: Point, Reason, Example, Point. Let us try.
pa.ipa_noi: /pɔɪnt ˈriːzən‿ɪˈɡzæmpəl pɔɪnt let‿əs traɪ/

luot.en: Point: Cities need money. Reason: Better roads.
luot.vi: Điểm chính: Thành phố cần tiền. Lý do: Đường sá tốt hơn.

pa.cau: Point: Cities need money. Reason: Better roads.
pa.ipa_noi: /pɔɪnt ˈsɪtiːz niːd ˈmʌni ˈriːzən ˈbetə rəʊdz/

luot.en: Example: The new metro line in Ha Noi.
luot.vi: Ví dụ: Tuyến tàu điện mới ở Hà Nội.

pa.cau: Example: The new metro line in Ha Noi.
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪˈɡzæmpəl ðə nuː ˈmeˌtrəʊ laɪn‿ɪn hɑː noi/

luot.en: Exactly. Point: It benefits the public long term.
luot.vi: Chính xác. Điểm chính: Nó có lợi cho cộng đồng lâu dài.

pa.cau: Exactly. Point: It benefits the public long term.
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪˈɡzæktliː pɔɪnt‿ɪt ˈbenəfɪts ðə ˈpʌblɪk lɔːŋ tɜːm/

luot.en: But what about the poor? That is my concern.
luot.vi: Nhưng còn người nghèo thì sao? Đó là mối bận tâm của tôi.

pa.cau: But what about the poor? That is my concern.
pa.ipa_noi: /bət‿wʌt‿əˈbaʊt ðə pʊə ðət‿ɪz maɪ kəˈnsɜːn/

luot.en: That is the main issue. We need better policy.
luot.vi: Đó là vấn đề chính. Chúng ta cần chính sách tốt hơn.

pa.cau: That is the main issue. We need better policy.
pa.ipa_noi: /ðət‿ɪz ðə meɪn ˈɪʃuː wiː niːd ˈbetə ˈpɑːləsiː/

luot.en: Do you think policy solves social problems fast?
luot.vi: Bạn có nghĩ chính sách giải quyết vấn đề xã hội nhanh không?

pa.cau: Do you think policy solves social problems fast?
pa.ipa_noi: /də jə θɪŋk ˈpɑːləsiː sɑːlvz ˈsəʊʃəl ˈprɑːbləmz fæst/

luot.en: It takes time. It is not like Part 1.
luot.vi: Cần thời gian. Nó không giống như Part 1 đâu.

pa.cau: It takes time. It is not like Part 1.
pa.ipa_noi: /ɪt teɪks taɪm‿ɪt‿ɪz nɑːt laɪk pɑːt/

luot.en: Yes, Part 3 needs more abstract thinking.
luot.vi: Vâng, Part 3 cần tư duy trừu tượng nhiều hơn.

pa.cau: Yes, Part 3 needs more abstract thinking.
pa.ipa_noi: /jes pɑːt niːdz mɔː æbˈstrækt ˈθɪŋkɪŋ/

luot.en: I think we are getting better at this.
luot.vi: Tôi nghĩ chúng ta đang làm tốt dần lên đấy.

pa.cau: I think we are getting better at this.
pa.ipa_noi: /aɪ θɪŋk‿wiː ə ˈɡetɪŋ ˈbetə ət ðɪs/

luot.en: I agree. Practice makes perfect in Speaking.
luot.vi: Tôi đồng ý. Luyện tập sẽ làm bài nói trở nên hoàn hảo.

pa.cau: I agree. Practice makes perfect in Speaking.
pa.ipa_noi: /aɪ əˈɡriː ˈpræktəs meɪks pəˈfekt‿ɪn ˈspiːkɪŋ/

luot.en: Let us continue this discussion tomorrow.
luot.vi: Hãy tiếp tục thảo luận này vào ngày mai nhé.

pa.cau: Let us continue this discussion tomorrow.

hoi_thoai.ten: Hội thoại — Văn hóa và công nghệ

luot.en: Does modern technology change our culture, Lan?
luot.vi: Công nghệ hiện đại có làm thay đổi văn hóa của chúng ta không Lan?

pa.cau: Does modern technology change our culture, Lan?
pa.ipa_noi: /dəz ˈmɑːdən teˈknɑːlədʒiː tʃeɪndʒ ˈaʊə ˈkʌltʃə læn/

luot.en: I think so. Traditional crafts are disappearing.
luot.vi: Tôi nghĩ vậy. Các nghề thủ công truyền thống đang dần biến mất.

pa.cau: I think so. Traditional crafts are disappearing.
pa.ipa_noi: /aɪ θɪŋk səʊ trəˈdɪʃənəl kræfts‿ə ˌdɪsəˈpɪrɪŋ/

luot.en: Can we use PREP to discuss this topic?
luot.vi: Chúng ta có thể dùng PREP để thảo luận chủ đề này không?

pa.cau: Can we use PREP to discuss this topic?

doan_van.ten: Đoạn văn mẫu — Lập luận trừu tượng trong Part 3
doan_van.noi_dung:
Unlike the personal and descriptive nature of Speaking Part 1, Part 2 demands a sustained narrative, whereas Part 3 requires candidates to engage in abstract reasoning and broader societal analysis. While earlier parts of the exam invite test takers to discuss their individual daily routines or personal preferences, Part 3 prompts them to evaluate dynamic global issues, consider historical changes, and speculate on hypothetical scenarios. To achieve a band score of 6.5 or higher, candidates must demonstrate their ability to move beyond simple personal anecdotes and articulate well-structured, generalised arguments that reflect a deeper understanding of complex topics.

A highly effective strategy for tackling these sophisticated questions is the structured PREP framework, which stands for Point, Reason, Example, and Point restatement. By first presenting a direct and clear thesis statement, candidates establish a firm, unambiguous position on the topic. Subsequently, explaining the underlying causes or logical mechanisms provides crucial conceptual depth to the response. Supporting these justifications with illustrative examples (drawn from dynamic economic trends or general cultural phenomena rather than private memories) further reinforces the validity of the central argument. Finally, succinctly summarizing the primary idea ensures that the overall discourse remains coherent, logical, and focused throughout the entire interaction.

Furthermore, candidate performance in Part 3 largely depends on their capacity to handle six distinct question types, ranging from evaluating potential advantages and predicting future developments to comparing contrasting perspectives and assessing solutions. Adapting one's response structure to these specific prompts requires linguistic flexibility and sophisticated lexical control. Rather than making sweeping, absolute assertions, successful candidates frequently employ cautious language, skillfully utilizing modal verbs and subtle hedging expressions to reflect the naturally complex and nuanced character of modern societal issues.

Ultimately, candidates must carefully balance the four key assessment criteria: Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Pronunciation. While advanced vocabulary is undeniably valuable, coherent logical progression and structural accuracy often determine whether a candidate successfully reaches the higher band thresholds. Developing the capability to construct abstract arguments systematically ultimately enables test takers to communicate complex, nuanced ideas with genuine confidence and academic precision.

doan_van.noi_dung: Working from home often provides a significant boost to individual productivity and personal well-being. Firstly, the elimination of a daily commute allows employees to reclaim valuable time, which they can invest in professional development or family life. Secondly, a controlled home environment reduces common workplace distractions, enabling individuals like Nam to focus deeply on complex tasks. Nam typically starts his workday at eight in the morning in his quiet study. He prepares a strong cup of coffee while reviewing his schedule for the upcoming afternoon meetings. The silence of the house fosters a sense of creative clarity that the office rarely affords. However, as the afternoon sun begins to fade, he realizes that the lack of social interaction creates a subtle sense of isolation. He decides to pack his laptop and head to a local café to finish his reports. The transformation from a solitary home worker to a social participant changes his entire outlook on the day. By the evening, he feels both intellectually accomplished and socially refreshed.

Nam returns home satisfied with his resilience despite the minor early disruption.

He eventually exchanges contact details with her to continue the dialogue later. luu_y:
**① Đừng trả lời quá ngắn.** *“Yes, I think so.”* rồi im — mất điểm Fluency ngay. Tối thiểu 4 câu.

**② Đừng trả lời quá dài.** Trên 90 giây/câu khiến giám khảo ngắt lời, và bạn dễ lạc đề.

**③ Không hiểu câu hỏi thì HỎI LẠI, đừng đoán:**
*Sorry, do you mean…? · Could you rephrase that, please?*

> Hỏi lại **không bị trừ điểm**. Trả lời lạc đề mới bị trừ.

**④ Đừng nói về bản thân trong Part 3.** Câu hỏi về xã hội. Được lấy trải nghiệm cá nhân làm **ví dụ**, nhưng quan điểm phải ở tầm chung.

**⑤ Câu giờ hợp lý** khi cần nghĩ:
*That’s a difficult question… · I’ve never really thought about it, but I suppose…*

> Tránh im lặng và tránh “ừm… ừm…” kéo dài.

**⑥ Phát âm quan trọng hơn từ vựng khó ở Part 3.** Nói từ đơn giản rõ ràng ăn điểm hơn nói từ hiếm mà giám khảo phải đoán.

mini_story.truyen: Working from home often provides a significant boost to individual productivity and personal well-being. Firstly, the elimination of a daily commute allows employees to reclaim valuable time, which they can invest in professional development or family life. Secondly, a controlled home environment reduces common workplace distractions, enabling individuals like Nam to focus deeply on complex tasks. Nam typically starts his workday at eight in the morning in his quiet study. He prepares a strong cup of coffee while reviewing his schedule for the upcoming afternoon meetings. The silence of the house fosters a sense of creative clarity that the office rarely affords. However, as the afternoon sun begins to fade, he realizes that the lack of social interaction creates a subtle sense of isolation. He decides to pack his laptop and head to a local café to finish his reports. The transformation from a solitary home worker to a social participant changes his entire outlook on the day. By the evening, he feels both intellectually accomplished and socially refreshed.

mini_story.truyen: Effective communication strategies are essential for building professional relationships during academic conferences. First, active listening allows individuals to grasp complex concepts without immediate judgment. Second, concise articulation ensures that thoughts remain coherent during high-stakes discussions. Nam attends a large seminar in London today to practise these skills. He feels nervous as he approaches a stranger named Elena near the coffee station. Nam initiates a conversation by asking about her research focus regarding climate change. Elena explains her methodology with passion while Nam listens intently to every word. Their exchange lasts for several minutes as they explore various abstract theories together. Slowly, his anxiety evaporates and he begins to feel confident in his social abilities. He eventually exchanges contact details with her to continue the dialogue later. Nam experiences a significant shift in his perspective towards networking and leaves the venue feeling genuinely inspired.
